text:
Amanda: Quick note — profiler surfaced a sharp tail when KV miss rate goes above ~12% during short bursts (4-8 tokens). Latency jumps + kernel selection churn. Thinking about a small staged decline window to avoid instant hard 429s and to keep batching stable. Thoughts?

Raj: saw the same on yesterday's canary. Kernel swap thrash when batches shrink unexpectedly. A gradual decline makes sense instead of instant shed. :+1:

Oliver: can you paste the flame snippet? curious where time is spent — kernel vs memory copy vs kv lookup.

Amanda: pasted quick snippet below (trimmed):
```
flame: serving_loop ~ 48%
  kernel_dispatch ~ 26%
    select_kernel_for_seqlen ~ 8%
    matmul_kernel ~ 12%
  kv_lookup ~ 14% (misses spiking)
  batching_overhead ~ 6%
```
This is from a 30s window during high small-burst traffic.

Linh: that kv_lookup spike matches a prefetch regression we rolled last week? if cache prefetch is delayed you get misses which reduce batch reuse and trigger kernel reroute.

Sophie: idea: staged-decline window = keep window open for X ms while monitoring effective batch size and kv-hit-rate. if burst recovers within window, continue. only start shedding after window expiry. also gradually lower token budget instead of immediate hard cut.

Raj: agree. concrete params to try: DECLINE_WINDOW_MS=150, GRACE_DECAY=0.75 (multiply token budget each step), STEP_MS=40, MIN_TOKEN_BUDGET=80. That lets a 200->80 budget ramp over ~3 steps rather than a single drop.

Amanda: prototype config I ran locally:
```json
{
  "decline_window_ms": 150,
  "step_ms": 40,
  "decay_factor": 0.75,
  "min_token_budget": 80,
  "check_kv_hit_threshold": 0.10
}
```
Result: tail p95->p99 reduced by ~22% on the test harness, no extra errors.

Oliver: nice. Did you see any change in kernel selection churn?

Amanda: yes — fewer mid-request kernel switches because batches stayed above the threshold for a few extra decisions. Kernel selection still triggered on larger seqlen variance but much less often during microbursts.

Linh: two followups: 1) tie decline-window expiry to a smoothed kv-hit % (ema over 200ms) rather than raw timer; 2) add an opt-in route-level override so product teams can choose aggressive vs gentle decline.

Sophie: we should also emit a new metric: staged_decline_step (0/1/2/3) per request so console can show how often we recover vs actually shed.

Raj: for routing fallback when we must shed, prefer switching to the quantized variant (q4-lite) that preserves output shape rather than dropping. Less user-visible error. Add a short cooldown per-client so we don't flip-flop.

Amanda: good call. sketch of logic: when step >= 2 AND kv-hit_rate < threshold -> route to q4-lite for next 200 requests; when kv-hit_rate recovers, ramp back gradually.

Sophie: can we simulate with the loadgen? do a replay with synthetic kv-miss bursts and check cost/regression.

Amanda: I'm running a 10 minute replay now with 60% small bursts and 15% forced kv misses. will post results.

sre-bot: deploy-preview: canary 20240308-quickdecline applied to cluster dev-rt-3. checks: ok.

Oliver: once Amanda posts numbers let's schedule a short experiment rollout to 10% traffic on staging. Keep an eye on error budget and p99.

Amanda: posted replay summary:
- baseline p99: 420ms
- staged-decline p99: 320ms
- error rate: +0.02% (due to routing to q4-lite, acceptable)
- kernel-switch events: down 45%

Raj: solid. next steps: add EMA kv-hit gating, metric for steps, route-level flags, and a unit test for step decay math. I'll pick up the unit tests.

Linh: I'll own dashboard widgets and alert thresholds for staged_decline_step > 1 sustained 30s.

Sophie: and I'll add a short note in the runbook explaining when to tune decline_window_ms vs decay_factor.

Amanda: thanks all. if no objections I'll queue a canary rollout to 5% tomorrow morning. :rocket:

Oliver: go for it.

Raj: lgtm.
